name: albanian_04
context: A Facebook comment under a post by the National Institute of Public Health of Kosovo during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The comment is in Albanian, mostly the informal Kosovo (Gheg) dialect, often written without the letters ë and ç.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 1 overcorrected. Negative recall fell from 159 to 83/171, with 88 negatives called neutral, and 34 positives were called neutral, mostly hopes for zero cases.

Patterns in the missed negatives:
- Blame: 'X i ka fajet' (X is to blame), 'qeveria koti' (the government of Kurti, used mockingly).
- Mocking the reported numbers as fabricated: copy paste, aparati (the machine).
- Fed-up frustration: bajat (stale), boll (enough), lodhet (tired).
- Insults to citizens or officials.
- Fear of catastrophe.
- Gloating sarcasm: e hupi kontrollen (it lost control).

Positive: annotators count hope and wishes for zero cases, and cheering of recoveries, as positive. Version 1's not_for line excluded these wishes, so I drop that exclusion.

I set a middle line. Negative needs blame, mockery, frustration, insult or fear. Neutral keeps data requests, practical demands, calm advice and light banter. I trimmed wording to stay under 400 words.

Version 3 scored 80.7 macro-F1. The remaining errors are balanced: 38 neutral→negative and 37 negative→neutral, many of them annotator noise, so I make only targeted tweaks.

Missed negatives fall into three groups:
- Insult or curse words the cue list lacked: magari (donkey), pisa (dirty one), flaka ju dalt (may you burn), ju raft (may it strike you), qeveria/Kotit (Kurti's government, used mockingly).
- Bitter irony that sounds positive or neutral on the surface: 'E vetmja gjë pozitive... jane qeto raste' (the only positive thing in this country is these cases), 'Si gjithcka tjeter... do te deshtoj' (like everything else, it will fail), 'Vdekjen e sfidon' (he defies death).
- Gloating that a city 'lost control' (e hupi kontrollen) and 'spo na intereson' (we don't care).
Some of these went to positive, so I add a not_for line: irony that praises something bad is negative.

Positive errors: polite, respectful comments signed 'Me respekt' (with respect) or opened 'Te nderuar' (dear sirs) are gold positive even when they mainly ask or suggest. 'Respekt..., por' (respect, but) is positive. I state that respectful courtesy counts as positive.

Neutral→positive errors: city-ranking banter ('Prishtina n Top form', 'kryesorja' (the leader)) and 'S'ashte keq' (not bad). I add these to positive's not_for.

Neutral→negative errors: long reasoned proposals or complaints about citizens, which the rule already says stay neutral. 'Katastrofe' overfired once, so I keep fear but require it to be the commenter's own feeling. I keep the structure of version 3.

Version 4 (79.8) did slightly worse than version 3 (80.7), so most of its additions did not help.
- The courtesy-is-positive rule ('Me respekt') did not recover those positives.
- The irony rule and the extra insult cues did not recover the hidden negatives, which stayed at about 44 (37 in version 3).
- 18 neutrals still went to positive.

The remaining errors are mostly noise: gold-neutral comments that insult the minister, and gold-negative jokes that look exactly like neutral banter.

One pattern is learnable. Gold-neutral comments the model calls negative are often long, serious complaints or demands aimed at citizens or the institute. They scold or accuse, but contain no insult, curse or fakery claim; examples are 'Rudina... rrini mren' (stay inside), 'Po shihet qe njerezit nuk jane te diciplinuar' (it's clear people aren't disciplined) and 'Ku jane komunat tjera... Pse po i fshehni' (where are the other municipalities... why are you hiding them). Gold negatives usually carry an insult, curse, mocking label or fed-up phrase.

I therefore return to version 3's structure and add three things:
1. An explicit statement that serious scolding, accusatory 'why' questions and calls for measures stay neutral without an insult, curse, fakery claim or fed-up phrase.
2. Keep the useful insult cues and the 'qeveria Koti' (Kurti's government, used mockingly) cue.
3. Drop the courtesy rule. Move city-ranking banter to positive's not_for, to cut neutral-to-positive errors.

Versions 3 and 5 both reach 80.7, so the boundaries have plateaued. Most remaining errors look like annotator noise: gold-neutral comments that insult the minister or accuse the institute of hiding cases, and gold-negative jokes that are indistinguishable from neutral banter. I make only narrow, learnable fixes.

1. Positive→negative: 'Në asnjë rast nuk mundemi ta fajsojm qeverin' (we can't blame the government at all) and 'qeveria koti po punon shum' (the Kurti government is working hard) defend or praise the government. The 'Koti' and 'faj' (blame) cues pushed them to negative. Fix: defending or praising the government or institute is positive, even when the comment blames citizens. The 'Koti' cue applies only when it is used mockingly.

2. Neutral→positive: ironic 'hajr' or 'ma gjall' over new case counts ('213 ja pafshim hajrin' (may we see good from these 213), 'Hajde ma gjall... 168' (come on, livelier, only 168)) and bare good-news headlines ('ASNJË RAST POZITIV NË PRIZREN' (no positive case in Prizren), 'S'ashte keq' (not bad)) are gold neutral. Fix: add these to positive's not_for.

3. Negative→positive: jokes that cheer on rising cases ('Min shtes naj rrasi goll' (add a goal or two), 'Sjeni tu dhez ma' (you're not on fire anymore)) and bitter irony ('do te deshtoj' (it will fail)). These are partly noise. I mention bitter irony about Kosovo failing as negative.

Everything else stays as in version 5.

Same plan as before. Version 6 narrowed negative blame to the authorities and lost negatives that blame citizens or gatherings, or that fear catastrophe. I restore blame of anyone and add fear of catastrophe, and keep version 6's positive fixes. Wording is trimmed to stay under 400 words.

Version 7 scored 79.5, below versions 3 and 5 (80.7).

Extending negative to blame of citizens and fear of catastrophe added 8 neutral→negative errors (42 vs 34) but recovered only 7 negatives. The new errors were serious scolding of citizens, proposals to fine people and 'katastrofe' (catastrophe) warnings, all gold neutral. So citizen-blame does not reliably signal negative here.

Positive recall also dropped to 84. Several missed positives share a learnable pattern: a bare name tag or a short phrase carrying a one-word approval, such as 'Ali Kastrati mire' (good), 'Muriqi Izi Muriqi super a' (super, right), 'Ylli Bunjaku nice', 'Agron Cocaj perher' (always), 'vazhdojm' (let's keep going), 'Rrnoft qaji me limon' (long live lemon tea) and 'Besnik Karaxha Perhajr na Koft' (may it be for the good). Annotators count these as positive, while bare tags stay neutral.

Plan:
- Return to version 5's negative boundary: blame, fake-number claims, insults or curses, fed-up statements, the commenter's own fear or despair. Serious scolding and proposals stay neutral.
- Keep version 6's fix that defending or praising the government is positive.
- Add the short-approval-word cue to positive.
- Keep the not_for for ironic 'hajr' and 'ma gjall' over case counts.

Version 9 is the best so far at 81.8, and its errors are balanced: 36 neutral→negative and 38 negative→neutral, mostly annotator noise. For the final version I make one minimal, safe tweak.

Gold-neutral headlines that simply report good news, such as 'ASNJË RAST POZITIV NË PRIZREN' (no positive case in Prizren), are still predicted positive. I put 'bare good-news headlines' back into positive's not_for; it had been cut to meet the word limit. To stay under 400 words, I drop two low-value cues: 'on top' from neutral (already covered by city banter in the rule) and 'deshtim' (failure) from negative. Everything else is unchanged.
